sources.title: Michael W. Davis, The Geometry and Topology of Coxeter Groups (Princeton University Press 2008, first-edition author manuscript PDF, 600 pages)
sources.locator: Sections read for this batch: Chapter 4, section 4.6 (Lemma 4.6.1 and Lemma 4.6.2 with proofs, printed pp. 51-53); Chapter 5, Example 5.2.7 and the opening of section 5.3 (the Coxeter complex U(W,Delta) and the common-coface property, printed pp. 66-68); Chapter 6, Theorem 6.4.3 with the induction (s_n)=>(c_{n+1})=>(t_{n+1}) (printed pp. 81-84), Theorem 6.6.3 with Lemmas 6.6.4-6.6.6 (printed pp. 87-92), section 6.8 (the cosine matrix and dihedral angles of a spherical simplex, printed pp. 96-102) and Theorem 6.12.9 (printed pp. 119-120); Appendix D.1 (Tits' Theorem D.1.1 and Corollaries D.1.2-D.1.3, printed pp. 439-441) and Appendix D.2 (Examples D.2.1, Lemmas D.2.2-D.2.5, Theorems D.2.6-D.2.7, printed pp. 442-447). Chapters 3 and the rest of Chapter 4 were not re-read here; the run's commissioned source report records their complete reading and remains the authority for the foundational results this page consumes.

contents.name: Chapter 4, Lemma 4.6.1: the equivalent conditions (a) l(w0)=l(u)+l(u^{-1}w0) for all u and (b) l(w0)>l(rw0) for all reflections r; w0 exists iff W is finite; uniqueness, l(w0)=Card(R), w0 an involution, w0Sw0=S
Chapter 4, Lemma 4.6.2: a single element w0 with l(sw0)<l(w0) for all simple s forces W finite and w0 longest

Chapter 5, Definition 5.2.6 and Example 5.2.7: the Coxeter complex U(W,Delta) as a simplicial complex; for finite W it is homeomorphic to a sphere (Theorems 6.4.3, 6.12.9 and Lemma 6.3.3); for infinite W it is contractible
Chapter 5, section 5.3: any two chambers of U(W,X) intersect in a common coface (possibly the empty coface)

Chapter 6, Theorem 6.4.3 and its proof: the developing map U(W,P^n)->X^n is a homeomorphism for a simple convex polytope with dihedral angles pi/m_ij; in the spherical case U(W,sigma^n) is homeomorphic to S^n and W is finite

Chapter 6, Theorem 6.6.3: for a finite group generated by linear reflections, (W,S) is a Coxeter system, W acts simply transitively on the chambers, the essential chamber is a simplicial cone and U(W,C)->R^n is a homeomorphism; Lemmas 6.6.4-6.6.6 give the gallery graph, the pre-reflection-system data and the simple-transitivity steps
Chapter 6, section 6.8: the Gram/cosine matrix of a spherical simplex and its dihedral angles; a spherical simplex with prescribed Gram matrix exists when the matrix is positive definite
Chapter 6, Theorem 6.12.9: W is a reflection group on S^{n-1} with a spherical-simplex fundamental chamber iff the cosine matrix is positive definite iff W is finite
Appendix D.1: Tits' Theorem D.1.1 (w(C-degree) intersect C-degree nonempty implies w=1) and Corollaries D.1.2-D.1.3 (faithfulness and discreteness of the canonical representation)
contents.reason: Dual-chamber disjointness, Tits' lemma and faithfulness of the canonical representation are already supplied and proved locally by the earlier batches 2, 4, 7 and 9 of this run; this page consumes their statements and mints no competing item for them.

contents.name: Appendix D.2: Lemma D.2.2 (side rule), Lemma D.2.3 and Corollary D.2.4 (y in the open opposite chamber lies in U iff W is finite; 0 is interior to U iff W is finite), Lemma D.2.5 (wx=y with x,y in C implies x=y and w in W_{S(x)}), Theorem D.2.6 (U(W,C)->U is a bijection, U(W,C^f)->I is a homeomorphism onto the interior), Theorem D.2.7 (U is convex)

Appendix D.2, Examples D.2.1: the infinite dihedral group (chamber the positive quadrant, the invariant affine line x1+x2=1 with the standard D-infinity action, C^f=C-{0}, U and I described there); Euclidean and hyperbolic analogues
contents.note: The source's sentence 'U is the half-plane x1+x2>=0' is inconsistent with its own Lemma D.2.3 and Corollary D.2.4 and with the direct computation: the boundary rays {Delta=0} are limits of chambers but lie outside every chamber, so the union is {Delta>0} union {0}. The example proves the correct statement locally and does not use that sentence; the correcting computation is recorded in the batch notes as an in-run defect finding against lem-cg-dual-action-and-chamber-faces-exist (3)(ii), whose infinite-m union claim has the same error.

sources.title: Jean Michel, Lectures on Coxeter groups (Beijing lecture notes, April-May 2014, author-hosted PDF, 15 pages)
sources.locator: Sections read in the extracted full text: section 4 on the longest element (Proposition 4.6 with proof, printed pp. 5-6); section 5 'Finite real reflection groups' (Lemma 5.1 on the unique reflection per wall, Lemma 5.2, Proposition 5.4 with the chamber bijection, the uniqueness of the chamber -C and -C=w0(C), Proposition 5.8, printed pp. 6-9); sections 5.10-5.12 (Theorem 5.9, Tits' Lemma 5.11, Lemma 5.12 on parabolics and I-reduced elements, printed pp. 9-12). Printed pp. 12-15 (the classification of finite Coxeter groups) were not re-read for this batch; batch 13 of this run records that reading.

contents.name: Section 4, Proposition 4.6: the three equivalent characterizations of the longest element (left descents, l(w0w)=l(w0)-l(w), maximal length); if it exists it is unique, an involution, and W is finite
Section 5, Lemma 5.1: each wall H of a finite reflection arrangement carries a unique reflection s_H of W

Section 5, Proposition 5.4: for a finite reflection group, the walls of a chamber generate W as a Coxeter system, W permutes the chambers simply transitively (every chamber is uniquely w(C)), the stabilizer of a point is generated by the walls through it, and the chamber pair (-C,C) is separated by all walls so that -C=w0(C)
Section 5, Proposition 5.8: the unit normals e_H of the walls of a chamber of an irreducible finite reflection group are linearly independent and B(e_H,e_H')=-cos(pi/m)

Sections 5.10-5.12: Theorem 5.9 (the geometric representation realizes every Coxeter matrix), Tits' Lemma 5.11 (w(C) meet C empty for w nonidentity) and Lemma 5.12 (parabolic subsystems, I-reduced elements and coset minima)
contents.reason: The geometric representation, Tits' lemma, faithfulness and the parabolic coset theory are supplied and proved locally by the earlier batches 2, 4, 7, 9 and 10 of this run; this page consumes their results without duplicating their proof homes.

contents.name: Sections 6-7: classification of finite Coxeter groups (spherical graphs and the list of types)
contents.reason: The finite classification is the subject of the earlier finite-Coxeter-diagrams pair (batch 13) of this run; this page only consumes its finite-type conclusion and neither re-proves nor extends the list.
